purpose: Changes made to the live mechanism during this attempt because execution refuted an earlier version of it, kept distinct from source claims, reproductions and strategy proposals.

mechanism_changes.title: A change that names no path is a malformed path, not an unknown status
mechanism_changes.found_by: tests/test_adversarial.py::ChangeStatusEvasionTest::test_a_none_path_is_refused, on the first full run of the adversarial suite
mechanism_changes.observed_defect: An ADD whose path was null was refused with DENY_UNKNOWN_STATUS. The refusal was correct but the reason code was wrong: the status was valid and the path was missing. A coordinator triaging that code would have looked for a git parsing fault instead of a malformed change record.
mechanism_changes.why_it_matters: The reason code is the only machine-readable output a gate produces. A misleading code sends recovery down the wrong path, and the acceptance contract requires exact evidence for every non-PASS outcome.
mechanism_changes.change: In OwnershipEngine._check_change, the fallback for a status-valid change that yields no checkable side now returns DENY_MALFORMED_PATH, attributed to the side the status would have written, with the offending path value in the detail.
mechanism_changes.false_completion_risk_if_unfixed: none: the write was refused either way

mechanism_changes.title: The deny-shadow advisory considers declared deny globs only
mechanism_changes.found_by: Running the audit against the real 67-owner registry in workstreams/po03/control/path-ownership.json while generating result/registry-audit.json
mechanism_changes.observed_defect: The audit emitted 144 DENY_SHADOWED_GRANT advisories and a 75753-byte artifact. Every one came from the implicit deny globs '**/.git/**' and '**/.gitmodules' intersecting a recursive 'dir/**' grant. That intersection is a theorem about the patterns, not a fact about the registry, so the advisory carried zero information and would have buried a real contradiction.
mechanism_changes.why_it_matters: An audit whose output is dominated by unavoidable findings trains its reader to ignore it. Signal-to-noise is a correctness property of a gate, not a cosmetic one.
mechanism_changes.change: detect_shadowed_grants now iterates declared_deny_globs rather than the full deny set, with the reasoning recorded in its docstring. Admission behaviour is unchanged: the implicit denies still refuse those paths.

measured_effect.information_lost: none: no advisory referenced a declared deny glob

mechanism_changes.title: A deny glob with no separator is flagged, because anchoring is fail-dangerous for denies
mechanism_changes.found_by: Reasoning about the dialect decision while writing result/limitations.json, then confirmed by executing the engine
mechanism_changes.observed_defect: Choosing the anchored pathspec dialect makes a grant narrower than a .gitignore-style author intends, which is safe because it authorises less. The same narrowing applied to a deny glob is unsafe: a bare 'secrets.json' deny protects only the repository root and silently permits 'units/a/secrets.json'. Nothing in the engine surfaced that asymmetry.
mechanism_changes.why_it_matters: A deny list that reads as broader than it is produces exactly the silent-permission failure the collision boundary exists to prevent, and it would only be discovered by the leak.
mechanism_changes.change: Added OwnershipEngine.detect_narrow_deny_patterns, included in audit(). It reports any declared deny glob containing no separator and not already starting with '**', naming the '**/<pattern>' repair. It is ADVISORY rather than blocking so it cannot fail an existing correct registry.
mechanism_changes.current_registry_effect: none: every declared deny glob in path-ownership.json contains a separator, so the seeded registry raises no advisory

mechanism_changes.title: The read-back record names the manifest path it actually read, not a truncated tail of it
mechanism_changes.found_by: Re-reading the pushed return document from a fresh bare clone of the branch tip bf32b0229c473aa1585da322e24e36047b376fe9
mechanism_changes.observed_defect: immutable_readback.py built its manifest_path label as str(manifest_path).split('workstreams/')[-1], which dropped the 'workstreams/' prefix along with everything before it. The committed record therefore reported 'po03/wave-a/units/wa-010/result/artifact-manifest.json', a path no commit in this repository carries, while the checks list two lines below reported the same file under its real path.
mechanism_changes.why_it_matters: A read-back record exists so a third party can re-run the verification. Every digest in it was correct, so no hash comparison could catch this: an independent verifier following the label would get 'fatal: path does not exist' and could not distinguish a mislabelled record from a missing artifact.
mechanism_changes.change: Extracted repo_relative_manifest_path, which returns the canonical repository-relative path when the manifest being verified is the unit's own and otherwise reports the given path verbatim rather than guessing at a repository root. The label is now the same constant the read-back check itself uses, so the two cannot diverge.
mechanism_changes.false_completion_risk_if_unfixed: a return that claims immutable read-back of a path that does not exist, which reads as verified and is not independently checkable

mechanism_changes.title: Figures restated in prose are checked against the structured fields they restate
mechanism_changes.found_by: Comparing the committed return document's acceptance_self_check text against its own structured fields after the DEF-PO03-WA-010-04 correction moved the payload
mechanism_changes.observed_defect: Three figures in the self-check prose still described the superseded payload: '29 changed paths from the immutable base' when the count was 30, and '28 artifacts totalling 317637 bytes' when the manifest totalled 319755. The structured fields were all correct. Nothing compared the two, so a regeneration that moved a number left the sentence describing it behind, and a proof-read missed it twice.
mechanism_changes.why_it_matters: The self-check is where a producer states why it believes it satisfied the contract. A coordinator reading stale figures there cannot tell a bookkeeping lag from a boundary breach, and the discrepancy discredits the figures that are right.
mechanism_changes.change: Added result/check_return_consistency.py. Twelve cross-field checks compare fields that must agree, including the read-back manifest label against the declared manifest path, and seven narrative checks require each restated figure to appear literally in the sentence restating it. The return generator now interpolates these figures from the manifest and the changed-path record instead of carrying literals.
mechanism_changes.limitation: The narrative checks are keyed to the assertions this unit writes. A reworded assertion is reported as MISSING_ASSERTION rather than silently skipped, but a figure restated in prose the rules do not name is not covered.

defects_and_rework.detail: test_a_grant_of_everything_collides_with_every_other_owner preregistered 5 overlap findings for a greedy '**' grant against the disjoint fixture. The engine reported 6. The engine was right: findings are emitted per colliding glob pair, and the controller holds three grants, so it contributes three findings rather than one.
defects_and_rework.resolution: Corrected the expectation to 6 and added an assertion that every finding involves the greedy owner, so the count is anchored to a stated rule rather than to a number.

defects_and_rework.detail: During the initial smoke check of the intersection procedure, 'a/b/**' and 'a/**/b' were expected to be disjoint. They share 'a/b/b'. The witness the engine returned was matched by both patterns, which showed the expectation was wrong rather than the engine.
defects_and_rework.resolution: No code change. The case is now asserted in the intended direction by test_double_star_crossing, and witness self-verification was kept as a standing property of every overlap finding.

defects_and_rework.detail: source-claims.json first recorded the producer's own HEAD under the key 'immutable_controller_base_commit'.
defects_and_rework.resolution: Split into immutable_controller_base_commit (the pinned f2bdb4908026f66e8450802bb15921be1f3c338d), an executed merge-base ancestry check, and producer_head_commit_at_generation.

defects_and_rework.detail: limitations.json entry L12 first claimed that result/build_evidence.py regenerates every JSON artifact byte-identically and that only test-output.txt drifts. Running the regeneration from a fresh clone of the pushed branch showed source-claims.json also drifts, by the single producer_head_commit_at_generation line.
defects_and_rework.found_by: Executing the determinism claim instead of asserting it: clone the pushed branch, re-run build_evidence.py, then 'git status --porcelain'.
defects_and_rework.resolution: L12 rewritten to name both drifting artifacts, to state that four of six regenerated artifacts were byte-identical, and to carry the measurement method. This correction is the reason for the second payload and return commit on this branch.

defects_and_rework.detail: The read-back record embedded in the first two returns reported manifest_path as 'po03/wave-a/units/wa-010/result/artifact-manifest.json'. Splitting the absolute path on 'workstreams/' consumed the prefix, so the label named a path that exists in no commit. Every digest and byte count in the same record was correct.
defects_and_rework.found_by: Verifying the pushed return from a fresh bare clone rather than from the producer's worktree, then checking the record's own path label against the paths it says it read
defects_and_rework.resolution: Fixed in MC-PO03-WA-010-04 and pinned by four recurrence tests. RC-X04 in the new consistency checker fails on the superseded document and passes on the corrected one.

defects_and_rework.detail: After the DEF-PO03-WA-010-04 correction moved the payload commit, three figures restated in acceptance_self_check prose still described the superseded payload: 29 changed paths where the count was 30, and 28 artifacts totalling 317637 bytes where the manifest totalled 319755. The corresponding structured fields were correct throughout, so no digest or read-back check could detect the disagreement.
defects_and_rework.found_by: Reading the pushed return back and comparing its prose against its own structured fields, which is now the RC-N rule family
defects_and_rework.resolution: Fixed in MC-PO03-WA-010-05: the generator interpolates the figures from the manifest and the changed-path record, and the checker refuses a return whose prose and fields disagree. This correction is the reason for the third payload and return commit on this branch.

design_decisions.decision: Implement the anchored ':(glob)' pathspec dialect and reject ambiguous patterns at compile time.
design_decisions.rejected_alternative: Accept .gitignore semantics, where a separator-free pattern matches a basename at any depth.
design_decisions.reason: The registry grants are root-relative. Supporting both dialects in one matcher would mean a grant's breadth depended on how it happened to be written.

design_decisions.decision: Trailing '**' matches one or more segments, so 'a/**' does not match a file named 'a'.
design_decisions.rejected_alternative: Treat trailing '**' as zero or more.
design_decisions.reason: Verified against git: 'abc/**' matches what is inside 'abc'. A file that shadows the subtree root is outside the grant, and tests/test_gitglob.py asserts git agrees.

design_decisions.decision: Refuse traversal, absolute, drive-letter, doubled-separator, backslash, quoted and control-character paths instead of normalising them.
design_decisions.rejected_alternative: Resolve '..' and compare the resolved path.
design_decisions.reason: Normalising makes the admitted path differ from the path the writer submitted. Refusing keeps the decision about exactly what was presented, and a git diff never reports these shapes anyway.

design_decisions.decision: Require 'git diff --name-status -z' and reject a quoted path.
design_decisions.reason: Without -z git escapes unusual paths, and a quoted path matches no glob, which would turn an out-of-scope write into a silent pass.

design_decisions.decision: Return a witness path for every overlap rather than a boolean.
design_decisions.rejected_alternative: Report only that two patterns intersect.
design_decisions.reason: A witness makes the finding checkable by a third party and by the test suite, so the detector cannot quietly regress into always reporting overlap.

design_decisions.decision: Require the presented fence token to equal the registered one, refusing both lower and higher.
design_decisions.reason: A token above the registry means the registry this gate is reading is stale, so the gate is not the authority it believes it is and must not admit the write.

design_decisions.decision: Check a rename on both sides and a copy only on its target.
design_decisions.reason: A rename deletes the source, so target-only checking would let a writer move a sibling's committed result away. A copy leaves the source intact, so requiring source ownership would wrongly forbid reading.
